title: Peacock's Principle as a Conservative Strategy
summary: The view that Peacock's principle of permanence has been invalidated by Hamilton's introduction of non-commutative algebras has always seemed rather odd, in light of Peacock's favorable reception of quaternions and the endorsement of his principle by Hamilton. But the view is not just odd; it is incorrect. In order to show this, I critically analyze Peacock's attempts to reject possible exceptions to his principle, like the factorial function and an infinite series due to Euler. Then I argue that the principle of permanence is best understood as an expression of a conservative strategy,…
